To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pore size of the microporous organosilica was controlled by the doping of fluorine, and the C3H6 and iso C4H8 selectivity was improved by the addition of the fluorine concentration.

F BTESM microporous membranes with precisely controlled pore sizes were fabricated via doping with fluorine, and these membranes showed excellent molecular sieving properties with C3/C4 separation and high hydrocarbon permeance for C3H8.
fluorine doped bis(triethoxy-silyl)methanes (BTESM)s were used to fabricate organosilica microporous membranes with controlled pore size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of F BTESM microporous membranes that have a precisely controlled pore size, which is a key factor for C3 C4 separation.
the preparation of organosilica based membranes with a controlled pore size and their hydrocarbon permeation characteristics.
the fabrication and characterization of F BTESM organosilica microporous membranes with controlled pore diameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the F BTESM membrane is a promising membrane for C3 C4 H2 hydrocarbon separation.

a F BTESM membrane with a high fluorine doping concentration (F/Si = 0.15, pore size 0.7 nm) exhibited the highest permeance for C3H8 (2.0 x 107 mol m2 s 1) and the best separation properties (C3H8/C3H6 = 1.8 and C3H8/C4H10 = 2.5) at 50 deg C.
the pore size of the organosilica F BTESM membrane can be controlled by the fluorine concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a precise control of the pore sizes of the F BTESM membrane and a hydrocarbon affinity to silica materials are important factors for controlling hydrocarbon permeation and N/C separation.
the pore size of organosilica derived membranes can be precisely controlled by doping fluorine into the organosilica precursors.

the pore size and hydrocarbon affinity can be independently controlled by the fluorine content in the organosilica network, and this would be useful to develop a new class of organosilica molecular sieving membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrocarbon separation properties can be controlled by the pore size and the hydrocarbon adsorption characteristics of the organosilica material.
the pore sizes and hydrocarbon permeation characteristics of organosilica can be controlled by fluorine doping.
the pore size and the hydrocarbon adsorption properties of organosilica derived membranes can be precisely controlled by doping with a fluorine source.
